candidate.answerReason: A constructed 30° right triangle has hypotenuse 20. Its isosceles relationship with AB makes its intersection with CD satisfy the defining 15° angle for E.

methods.label: Construct a 30° triangle
methods.explanation:
The rectangle's height \(AD=10\) is half its width \(AB=20\). This suggests constructing a \(30^\circ\) right triangle with hypotenuse \(20\), then checking whether its endpoint is \(E\).

Draw a ray from \(A\) making \(30^\circ\) with \(AB\), toward the interior of the rectangle, and let it meet the ray \(DC\) at \(F\). Because \(AD\perp DF\), triangle \(ADF\) is right. Its angle at \(A\) is \(60^\circ\), so its angle at \(F\) is \(30^\circ\). The side opposite \(30^\circ\) is half the hypotenuse, giving
\[
AF=2AD=20.
\]
Also, \(DF\) is shorter than the hypotenuse \(AF=20=DC\), so \(F\) lies on the segment \(DC\).

Now \(AF=AB\), so triangle \(ABF\) is isosceles with vertex angle \(\angle BAF=30^\circ\). Its base angles are
\[
\angle ABF=\frac{180^\circ-30^\circ}{2}=75^\circ.
\]
Since \(\angle ABC=90^\circ\), this gives \(\angle CBF=15^\circ\). There is only one ray inside \(\angle ABC\) making \(15^\circ\) with \(BC\), so \(BF\) is the given ray \(BE\). Its intersection with \(CD\) is therefore \(F=E\).

Consequently, \(AE=AF=\boxed{20}\), choice E.
